sentences.en: Against all odds, Sidney Poitier, the first Black man to win an Academy Award, changed American cinema.
sentences.zh: 克服重重困难，第一位获得奥斯卡奖的黑人男演员西德尼·波蒂埃改变了美国电影。

sentences.en: But Wesley Morris, a culture critic at the Times, said it went further than that, that Poitier transformed America itself.
sentences.zh: 但《纽约时报》的文化评论员韦斯利·莫里斯表示，事情远不止于此，波蒂埃改变了美国本身。

sentences.en: It's Friday, January 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月14日，星期五。

sentences.en: Wesley, when Sidney Poitier died, you sat down and you wrote an essay about him.
sentences.zh: 韦斯利，在西德尼·波蒂埃逝世时，你坐下来写了一篇关于他的文章。

sentences.en: And I wonder if you can read the opening words of that essay.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否朗读一下那篇文章的开头。

sentences.en: Uh, one second, please.
sentences.zh: 嗯，请等一下。

sentences.en: Um, okay.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好的。

sentences.en: On January 7th, 2022, I, Wesley Morris, wrote, Were anyone to ask me who's the greatest American movie star, my answer would never change.
sentences.zh: 2022年1月7日，我，韦斯利·莫里斯写道，如果有人问我谁是美国最伟大的电影明星，我的答案永远不会改变。

sentences.en: And it will never change because the answer is easy.
sentences.zh: 而且它永远不会改变，因为答案很简单。

sentences.en: The greatest American movie star is Sidney Poitier.
sentences.zh: 美国最伟大的电影明星是西德尼·波蒂埃。

sentences.en: You mean the greatest Black movie star?
sentences.zh: 你是说最伟大的黑人电影明星？

sentences.en: I don't.
sentences.zh: 我不是那个意思。

sentences.en: Am I being controversial?
sentences.zh: 我有争议性吗？

sentences.en: Confrontational?
sentences.zh: 有对抗性吗？

sentences.en: Contrarian?
sentences.zh: 唱反调吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm simply telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 不，我只是在说实话。

sentences.en: That's a big paragraph.
sentences.zh: 那是一个很大的段落。

sentences.en: And it's a bold statement.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大胆的声明。

sentences.en: You only get to utter a sentence like that once, truly, in the life of a critic.
sentences.zh: 在评论员的一生中，你真的只有一次机会说出这样的话。

sentences.en: You said that Sidney Poitier is the greatest American movie star, period.
sentences.zh: 你说西德尼·波蒂埃是美国最伟大的电影明星，句号。

sentences.en: Can't be anybody else.
sentences.zh: 不可能是别人。

sentences.en: But listen, I don't think it's John Wayne.
sentences.zh: 但听着，我不认为是约翰·韦恩。

sentences.en: The case can be made.
sentences.zh: 这是可以辩论的。

sentences.en: I don't think it's Cary Grant.
sentences.zh: 我不认为是加里·格兰特。

sentences.en: The case can be made.
sentences.zh: 这也是可以辩论的。

sentences.en: I don't think it's Marilyn Monroe.
sentences.zh: 我不认为是玛丽莲·梦露。

sentences.en: The case can be made.
sentences.zh: 这也是可以辩论的。

sentences.en: My case is for Sidney
sentences.zh: 我支持西德尼·

sentences.en: Poitier.
sentences.zh: 波蒂埃。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: I can't think of another person who had to mean more to do more just to be taken seriously in a movie in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我想不出另一个人，为了在一部电影中首先被认真对待，必须付出更多意义、做更多的事情。

sentences.en: You know, he was working in a hole where other actors were at sea level.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是在一个深坑里工作，而其他演员都在海平面上。

sentences.en: So there's that.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样。

sentences.en: There's also the fact that, you know, he was asked to do a very specific thing over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 还有这样一个事实，你知道，他被要求一遍又一遍地做一件非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Which is?
sentences.zh: 是什么？

sentences.en: He was changing the way people saw a people who for 120 years at that point in the 1950s were only looking at Black people one way.
sentences.zh: 他在改变人们看待一种人的方式，在20世纪50年代的那个时候，这种人已经有120年只被黑人以一种方式看待了。

sentences.en: They had not been trained to see a Black person be physically equal in stature in a movie to a white man.
sentences.zh: 他们没有受过训练，去看到一个黑人在电影中与白人在身材上处于平等的地位。

sentences.en: They hadn't seen a Black man share uncontested space with a white woman.
sentences.zh: 他们没有见过一个黑人与一个白人女性毫无争议地共享空间。

sentences.en: They hadn't seen a Black man do anything professional that required training and skill and schooling until he showed up.
sentences.zh: 在他出现之前，他们没有见过黑人做过任何需要训练、技能和学校教育的专业工作。

sentences.en: So Wesley, walk us through the story of how Sidney Poitier came to be this thing, in your words, the greatest American movie star.
sentences.zh: 所以韦斯利，请用你的话带我们了解西德尼·波蒂埃如何成为这样一个人，即美国最伟大的电影明星的故事。

sentences.en: Where does that story start?
sentences.zh: 这个故事从哪里开始？

sentences.en: It starts about as far away from the movies as you could possibly get.
sentences.zh: 它开始于离电影尽可能远的地方。

sentences.en: Cat Island was like a garden.
sentences.zh: 卡特岛就像一个花园。

sentences.en: Fruit grew on trees.
sentences.zh: 水果长在树上。

sentences.en: He grew up in the Bahamas.
sentences.zh: 他在巴哈马长大。

sentences.en: My father was a tomato farmer.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是一个西红柿农场主。

sentences.en: His father Reginald and his mother Evelyn grew and sold tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲雷吉纳德和母亲伊夫琳种植并出售西红柿。

sentences.en: And they struggled.
sentences.zh: 他们挣扎求生。

sentences.en: They were poor and had a hard time making ends meet.
sentences.zh: 他们很穷，很难维持生计。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of need.
sentences.zh: 有很多需求。

sentences.en: We're talking about a large family.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是一个大家庭。

sentences.en: And Sidney was getting into trouble.
sentences.zh: 西德尼开始惹麻烦了。

sentences.en: And his father sees all of this and decides that it just might make more sense to lighten the family's load to ship him somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲看到了这一切，决定减轻家庭的负担，把他送到别的地方去可能是更有意义的。

sentences.en: And that somewhere else is where his brother Cyril lives with his family, in Miami.
sentences.zh: 而那个别的地方就是他的兄弟西里尔和家人居住的地方，在迈阿密。

sentences.en: I didn't spend the first 15 years of my life cringing in the presence of white people.
sentences.zh: 我人生中的前15年并没有在白人面前感到畏缩。

sentences.en: And just to make it super clear so we understand what the Bahamas actually is, it is a Black country.
sentences.zh: 为了超级清楚地让我们明白巴哈马实际上是什么，它是一个黑人国家。

sentences.en: So, I grew up those 15 years.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在那15年里长大。

sentences.en: I was within the circumference of the Black community constantly.
sentences.zh: 我一直都在黑人群体的范围内。

sentences.en: So, you would be seeing as a Black person, Black people doing everything.
sentences.zh: 所以，你会看到作为一个黑人，黑人做着所有的事情。

sentences.en: It was an environment that nurtured me in ways that I wasn't even aware of.
sentences.zh: 那是一个以我甚至没有意识到的方式培育我的环境。

sentences.en: So, that I got to 15.
sentences.zh: 所以我到了15岁。

sentences.en: Not afraid of white people.
sentences.zh: 不怕白人。

sentences.en: So, to come to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以来到美国

sentences.en: and to suddenly, everywhere you go, your Blackness, the thing that was sort of nondescript and unremarkable, where you grew up, is suddenly a cause for alarm, a target for abuse.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，无论你走到哪里，你的黑人身份，在你长大地方那种不值一提、微不足道的东西，突然成了惊慌失措的原因，成了虐待的目标。

sentences.en: And frankly, to you, if you're Sidney Poitier, a complete and total mystery.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，对于你，如果你是西德尼·波蒂埃，这是一个完全彻底的谜。

sentences.en: Like, what is going on here?
sentences.zh: 就像，这里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And what did that look like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样子的？

sentences.en: I hated Florida.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌佛罗里达。

sentences.en: I hated Florida.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌佛罗里达。

sentences.en: I hated it because it was an unfair place.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌它，因为它是一个不公平的地方。

sentences.en: Well, it looked like segregation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它看起来就像种族隔离。

sentences.en: It looked like classic Jim Crow nonsense.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像经典的吉姆·克劳法案的胡闹。

sentences.en: And so, he decides that he is going to go as far away from that as he possibly can.
sentences.zh: 因此，他决定尽可能远离那个地方。

sentences.en: And as far away as he could deduce at that time was New York City.
sentences.zh: 根据他当时所能推断的，最远的地方就是纽约市。

sentences.en: I was in New York.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约。

sentences.en: I had three bucks.
sentences.zh: 我有三美元。

sentences.en: I had no friends, no family, no relations, no addresses.
sentences.zh: 我没有朋友，没有家庭，没有亲戚，没有地址。

sentences.en: I knew no one.
sentences.zh: 我不认识任何人。

sentences.en: I got off at the bus station of 50th Street and 8th Avenue.
sentences.zh: 我在50街和8大道交汇处的公共汽车站下了车。

sentences.en: I'm walking up and down Broadway.
sentences.zh: 我在百老汇走来走去。

sentences.en: I am absolutely, I am transfixed by the lights and the traffic and the people.
sentences.zh: 我绝对，我被灯光、交通和人群迷住了。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Absolutely incredible.
sentences.zh: 绝对不可思议。

sentences.en: So, he comes here, has this dream of, like, living in Harlem and having this great life.
sentences.zh: 所以，他来到这里，有这样的梦想，比如住在哈林区，过着美好的生活。

sentences.en: And he doesn't have a great life.
sentences.zh: 他并没有过上美好的生活。

sentences.en: He's essentially homeless, sleeping on a bench, arrested for vagrancy.
sentences.zh: 他基本上无家可归，睡在长椅上，因流浪罪被捕。

sentences.en: You know, he does a stint in the army, hates it, leaves, gets back to New York.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他在军队服役了一段时间，讨厌它，离开并回到了纽约。

sentences.en: And one day, he's scanning the Amsterdam News, the great black Harlem publication.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他在浏览哈林区伟大的黑人出版物《阿姆斯特丹新闻》。

sentences.en: And there's an ad for auditions at the American Negro Theater.
sentences.zh: 上面有一则美国黑人剧院试镜的广告。

sentences.en: And he decides he's going to show up to read, even though he knows he's not the best reader at this point.
sentences.zh: 他决定去朗读试镜，尽管他知道此时自己并不是最好的朗读员。

sentences.en: He's only had a little bit of schooling.
sentences.zh: 他只接受过一点点学校教育。

sentences.en: He said, oh, you're an actor?
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，你是个演员？

sentences.en: I said, yes, of course I am.
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，我当然是。

sentences.en: He said, okay.
sentences.zh: 他说，好的。

sentences.en: He said, here.
sentences.zh: 他说，给你。

sentences.en: He gave me a script, first time I had seen such a thing.
sentences.zh: 他给了我一个剧本，这是我第一次见到这样的东西。

sentences.en: And I started to read like this.
sentences.zh: 我开始这样读。

sentences.en: So, I want you to, that's about as far as I got.
sentences.zh: 所以我想让你，我差不多就读到这里。

sentences.en: And he is shown the door by this man.
sentences.zh: 然后这个人把他请了出去。

sentences.en: And on the way out of the door, the man basically tells him,
sentences.zh: 在出门的路上，这个人基本上告诉他，

sentences.en: no, this will never do.
sentences.zh: 不，这样绝对不行。

sentences.en: You don't have a future here.
sentences.zh: 你在这里没有前途。

sentences.en: No, sir.
sentences.zh: 不，先生。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: And as he tossed me out, he said something that changed my whole life.
sentences.zh: 当他把我扔出去时，他说了一句话，改变了我的一生。

sentences.en: He said, stop wasting people's time.
sentences.zh: 他说，别浪费别人的时间了。

sentences.en: Why don't you go out and get yourself a job as a dishwasher or something?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不出去找份洗碗工之类的工作呢？

sentences.en: And Poitier is like, excuse me?
sentences.zh: 波蒂埃心想，对不起？

sentences.en: I didn't come here to wash dishes.
sentences.zh: 我来这里不是为了洗碗的。

sentences.en: I didn't come here for any of that.
sentences.zh: 我来这里不是为了这些。

sentences.en: I came here to learn how to act, to join this acting group.
sentences.zh: 我是来学习如何表演，加入这个表演团体的。

sentences.en: And you're telling me that all I'm qualified to do is wash dishes?
sentences.zh: 而你却告诉我，我有资格做的全部事情就是洗碗？

sentences.en: By the time I reached the corner, I had resolved that I would become an actor to prove to him that I was not just destined to be a dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 当我走到街角时，我下定决心要成为一名演员，向他证明我不仅仅注定是一个洗碗工。

sentences.en: I mean, he became an actor out of personal offense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他出于个人的冒犯而成为了一名演员。

sentences.en: It was not a dream.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个梦想。

sentences.en: It wasn't an ambition.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个野心。

sentences.en: It was to prove somebody wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是为了证明某人是错的。

sentences.en: I think he wanted to prove that he was more than this country at this point in his life was telling him he could be.
sentences.zh: 我想他想证明，他不仅仅是当时生活中的这个国家告诉他可以成为的那种人。

sentences.en: So, ironically, he decides that he is going to go back to the American Negro Theater and propose something.
sentences.zh: 所以，具有讽刺意味的是，他决定回到美国黑人剧院并提出一个建议。

sentences.en: And what he proposes is that he is going to basically be the maintenance guy for them if they let him watch the acting lessons and watch the productions.
sentences.zh: 他的提议是，如果他们让他观看表演课和观看制作，他基本上会成为他们的维修工。

sentences.en: And he gets an education in how to carry himself, how to interpret lines, how to stand on stage, how to take direction.
sentences.zh: 他接受了如何举止、如何诠释台词、如何在舞台上站立、如何接受导演指导的教育。

sentences.en: And he works really hard to lose his West Indian accent, listens to a lot of radio to lose it.
sentences.zh: 他非常努力地改掉他的西印度群岛口音，听了大量的广播来改掉它。

sentences.en: And that beautiful, what I would still say is just like a beautifully melodic speaking voice is born.
sentences.zh: 那个美丽的、我仍然要说是像极其优美的富有旋律的说话声音诞生了。

sentences.en: And he learns to speak a kind of American entertainment English.
sentences.zh: 他学会了说一种美国娱乐英语。

sentences.en: And he really begins to understand that he just knows what he does not want to be doing if he does get an opportunity to do something greater.
sentences.zh: 他真正开始明白，如果他确实有机会做更伟大的事情，他只是知道自己不想做什么。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, none of the actors who know Black actor during this period is like, you know what I really want to do?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这个时期，没有一个了解黑人演员的演员会说，你知道我真正想做的是什么吗？

sentences.en: I want to carry Jane Wyman's bags.
sentences.zh: 我想拎简·怀曼的包。

sentences.en: That's what I want to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想做的。

sentences.en: But I think that never taking a job, an acting job where that is what you do, is a totally different thing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，绝不接受一份那种正是你所做的工作的演艺工作，是完全不同的事情。

sentences.en: And there are lots of actors who didn't do that as well, and they didn't work.
sentences.zh: 也有很多演员没有那样做，他们没有工作。

sentences.en: And he is lucky enough and talented enough.
sentences.zh: 他足够幸运，也足够有才华。

sentences.en: I mean, you need both those things to make this Sidney Poitier adventure happen in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你需要这两样东西才能让西德尼·波蒂埃的这场冒险首先发生。

sentences.en: He starts getting parts that aren't the usual parts Black actors are even asked to play.
sentences.zh: 他开始得到甚至不是黑人演员通常被要求扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Don't touch the dressings.
sentences.zh: 别碰那些绷带。

sentences.en: I'll do that myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己来。

sentences.en: All righty, doctor.
sentences.zh: 好的，医生。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: One of them's a doctor in a movie called No Way Out from 1950.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是1950年电影《无路可走》里的医生。

sentences.en: He plays a priest in Cry the Beloved Country, that adaptation of that Alan Patton classic.
sentences.zh: 他在《啼笑皆非》中饰演一位牧师，那是根据艾伦·帕顿经典作品改编的电影。

sentences.en: Hey, Miller?
sentences.zh: 嘿，米勒？

sentences.en: Come on, I want to talk to you a minute, Miller.
sentences.zh: 来吧，我想跟你谈一会儿，米勒。

sentences.en: And then in 1955, he plays a student in this film called The Blackboard Jungle, where these teenage boys are just essentially terrorists at this high school.
sentences.zh: 然后是在1955年，他在一部名为《黑板从林》的电影中饰演一名学生，片中的那些十几岁男孩简直就是这所高中的恐怖分子。

sentences.en: And he's recruited to reform the bad boys.
sentences.zh: 而他被招募来改造这些坏男孩。

sentences.en: You know that you're a little brighter, a little smarter than the rest of those guys.
sentences.zh: 你知道自己比这群人里的其他人要更聪明、更有才华一点。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in all three of these movies, he is essentially this exceptional Negro.
sentences.zh: 所以在所有这三部电影中，他基本上都是这种非凡的黑人。

sentences.en: And a lot of his career, two major lanes of his career, are taken up with doctor parts and educator parts.
sentences.zh: 而他的职业生涯中，有两个主要的方向，都被医生角色和教育家角色所占据。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's an accident.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这绝非偶然。

sentences.en: I think that his assignment, his mandate, is essentially to heal and educate.
sentences.zh: 我认为他的使命、他的任务，本质上就是治愈和教育。

sentences.en: And anybody who comes to see him is essentially being healed in some ways or treated for their blindness to the humanity of black people and educated about what all black people can be and do.
sentences.zh: 任何来看他的人，在某种程度上本质上都是在被治愈，或是被治疗他们对黑人的人性的盲目，并被教育去了解所有黑人能够成为什么样的人、能做什么样的事。

sentences.en: And that is a huge shift from the way things were happening before Sidney Poitier got to the movies.
sentences.zh: 这与西德尼·波蒂埃涉足电影之前的情况相比，是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's not easy to undo 120 years of racist images of black people as servile, as stupid, as hopelessly happy to be enslaved.
sentences.zh: 要消除120年来将黑人描绘成卑躬屈膝、愚蠢至极、甘愿沦为奴隶的种族主义形象，这并不容易。

sentences.en: It's impossible to undo.
sentences.zh: 这根本无法消除。

sentences.en: We have not undone it.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有消除它。

sentences.en: But when Sidney Poitier shows up, it is a seismic shift away from what had previously been happening in the movies before he got there.
sentences.zh: 但当西德尼·波蒂埃出现时，它带来了震撼性的转变，彻底告别了他到来之前电影中一直发生的事情。

sentences.en: He wasn't the first person to try to do it.
sentences.zh: 他并不是第一个尝试这样做的人。

sentences.en: But the parts weren't as insulting now.
sentences.zh: 但现在这些角色不再那么具有侮辱性了。

sentences.en: And when you're a movie star, you can do a lot with a little.
sentences.zh: 当你成为电影明星时，你可以用少量的素材做出很多成就。

sentences.en: And nobody did more with less, I would say, in the history of American stardom than Sidney Poitier.
sentences.zh: 而且我想说，在美利坚明星的历史上，没有人能用这么少的筹码做到这么多，除了西德尼·波蒂埃。

sentences.en: Well, see,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你看，

sentences.en: I wonder if you can walk us through a particular performance in this early phase of his career where he embodies this idea you're describing of the very difficult work of undoing decades of perceptions of blackness and what it's supposed to look like on screen and being so very talented at doing it.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否带我们回顾一下他职业生涯早期的一部特定表演，在那部作品中，他具体体现了你所描述的这种理念：即极其艰难地去消除数十年对黑人群体的成见，去改变银幕上黑人应有的模样，并且在做这件事时表现得如此才华横溢。

sentences.en: You're tired, ain't you, baby?
sentences.zh: 你累了，对吧，宝贝？

sentences.en: You're oh so tired of everything.
sentences.zh: 你对一切都感到厌倦，噢，厌倦极了。

sentences.en: Me, the boy, the way we live in this beat up hole.
sentences.zh: 我，这个男孩，我们在这个破洞里生活的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, a raisin in the sun.
sentences.zh: 我是说，《阳光下的葡萄干》。

sentences.zh: 我是说，你不可能无缘无故站在我这边这么久。

sentences.en: A raisin in the sun.
sentences.zh: 《阳光下的葡萄干》。

sentences.en: Underrated movie, one of the first great works of American theater that is also written by a black person, in this case, Lorraine Hansberry.
sentences.zh: 被低估的电影，美国戏剧史上第一部伟大的作品之一，也是由黑人（本案中为洛林·汉斯贝里）创作的。

sentences.en: And when we're thinking about this idea of Sidney Poitier undoing so much screen history, so much entertainment history with respect to black people,
sentences.zh: 当我们思考西德尼·波蒂埃如何消解了关于黑人的如此多的银幕历史、如此多的娱乐历史时，

sentences.en: the thing about this performance and this part is that he is playing a driver.
sentences.zh: 关于这部表演和这个角色，奇妙之处在于他饰演的是一名司机。

sentences.en: And the thing that's amazing about it is you never really see him doing his job.
sentences.zh: 而最神奇的是，你从未真正看到他在做他的工作。

sentences.zh: 通常情况下，你看到的会是一个人开着车载着白人到处转悠。

sentences.en: I'm looking in the mirror this morning, I'm thinking I'm 35 years old, I'm married 11 years, and I got a boy who's got to sleep in the living room because I got nothing, hey?
sentences.zh: 我今天早上照镜子时想，我都35岁了，结婚11年了，还有一个必须睡在客厅里的儿子，因为我一无所有，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Michael, just to give you a sense of how bad things were for black people on screens and on stages by 1961,
sentences.zh: 我是说，迈克尔，为了让你了解1961年黑人在银幕和舞台上的处境有多糟糕，

sentences.en: this is a revolutionary act sitting in the home that a black woman created for black characters to sit and talk in.
sentences.zh: 坐在由一位黑人女性为黑人角色打造、供其落座交谈的家中，这是一种革命性的行为。

sentences.en: To show the fullness of a black character in his home environment.
sentences.zh: 展现一个黑人角色在其家庭环境中的完整性。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, when you put it that way, it sounds intentionally political.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，当你这么说时，听起来像是故意带有政治色彩的。

sentences.en: And obviously in 1961, it would have been.
sentences.zh: 显然在1961年，它确实如此。

sentences.en: But just think about the fact that, like, this is a human being wanting to write about human beings.
sentences.zh: 但只要想想这个事实：这是一个渴望书写人类的人类。

sentences.en: And where do human beings live?
sentences.zh: 而人类住在哪里？

sentences.en: In a house.
sentences.zh: 住在房子里。

sentences.en: A man say to his woman, I got me a dream.
sentences.zh: 一个男人对他的女人说，我有一个梦想。

sentences.en: She says, eat your eggs, they're getting cold.
sentences.zh: 她说，吃你的鸡蛋吧，它们快凉了。

sentences.en: I tell you, I got to change my life because I'm choking to death and all you say to me is eat these eggs.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，我必须改变我的生活，因为我快要窒息了，而你对我说的话只有吃这些鸡蛋。

sentences.en: And so the movie is about a family in Chicago living in a little apartment.
sentences.zh: 所以这部电影讲述的是芝加哥一个住在小公寓里的家庭。

sentences.en: There are five of them.
sentences.zh: 他们有五口人。

sentences.en: And they inherit $10,000.
sentences.zh: 他们继承了一万美元。

sentences.en: And the question, the central drama is, how do we spend this money?
sentences.zh: 而问题、核心的戏剧冲突是：我们该如何花这笔钱？

sentences.en: The mother, Lena Younger, wants to use the money to buy a house in a better neighborhood that is also white.
sentences.zh: 母亲莉娜·杨格想用这笔钱在条件更好、同时也是白人社区的地方买栋房子。

sentences.en: And one of the tensions that comes up is that, you know, they move to buy this house and the neighborhood, Clybourne Park in Chicago,
sentences.zh: 冲突之一就是，你知道的，当他们着手买下这栋房子和位于芝加哥的这个社区——克莱本公园时，

sentences.en: they dispatch a neighborhood improvement association representative to essentially buy them out of the house.
sentences.zh: 他们派出了一个社区改善协会的代表来，实质上是要把他们买出这栋房子。

sentences.en: To just, like, say, please don't do this.
sentences.zh: 也就是直截了当的说，请别这样做。

sentences.en: Don't move to this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 不要搬到这个社区来。

sentences.en: And the mother says, we shouldn't take this money.
sentences.zh: 母亲说，我们不应该拿这笔钱。

sentences.en: This is racist money.
sentences.zh: 这是充满种族主义的钱。

sentences.en: We shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 我们不该拿。

sentences.en: This is beneath us.
sentences.zh: 这有失我们的身份。

sentences.en: And the son, Walter, is played by Sidney Poitier, says, he who takes the most is the smarteSt.
sentences.zh: 而由西德尼·波蒂埃饰演的儿子沃尔特则说，拿最多的人才是最聪明的。

sentences.en: Absolutely, we should take this money.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们应该拿这笔钱。

sentences.en: Some awful pain.
sentences.zh: 阵阵剧烈的痛苦。

sentences.en: Don't cry.
sentences.zh: 别哭。

sentences.en: Just understand that that white man is going to walk in that door able to write checks for more money than we ever had.
sentences.zh: 只要明白那个白人走进这扇门时，他开出的支票金额会比我们见过的任何钱都多。

sentences.en: It's that important to him.
sentences.zh: 这对他是如此重要。

sentences.en: And we're going to help him.
sentences.zh: 而我们将去协助他。

sentences.en: We're going to put on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们要上演这场戏。

sentences.en: The speech that he gives and the way he delivers it with, you know, his arms and legs.
sentences.zh: 他的台词以及他用双臂和双腿去呈现它的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, he is using his whole body.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他在调动他的全身。

sentences.en: I didn't make this world.
sentences.zh: 我没有创造这个世界。

sentences.en: It was handed to me exactly like it is.
sentences.zh: 它原封不动地交到了我手里。

sentences.en: Yes, I want some yacht someday.
sentences.zh: 没错，我总有一天想要一艘游艇。

sentences.en: What's wrong with that?
sentences.zh: 这有什么不对？

sentences.en: And I want to put some pearls on my wife's neck.
sentences.zh: 我还想给我妻子的脖子上戴上珍珠项链。

sentences.en: You tell me what man decides in this world what woman should wear pearls and what woman shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 你告诉我，这个世界上是哪个男人决定哪个女人该戴珍珠，哪个女人不该戴的。

sentences.en: I tell you, I'm a man.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，我是个男人。

sentences.en: I say, I want her to wear it.
sentences.zh: 我说，我要让她戴。

sentences.en: There's something about all of this anger and threatened hope that he feels coming off of him.
sentences.zh: 他身上散发出的那种愤怒与受到威胁的希望，有着某种说不清道不明的意味。

sentences.zh: 你想维持现状吗？

sentences.zh: 你有权维持现状。

sentences.en: Fine.

sentences.zh: 那种灼热的 intensidad（强度）以及机敏与羞耻之间的转换如此生动。

sentences.zh: 也许我会双膝跪下，像个黑奴一样。

sentences.zh: 好吧，查理先生。

sentences.zh: 你们只要把钱给我们，我们就不会去那里弄脏你们白人的社区。

sentences.en: And at the center of that is Sidney Poitier.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的核心就是西德尼·波蒂埃。

sentences.en: And he only got more popular as the decade went on.
sentences.zh: 随着十年代的推进，他变得越来越受欢迎。

sentences.en: He wins the Oscar in 64.
sentences.zh: 他在64年赢得了奥斯卡。

sentences.en: He has massive hits after that.
sentences.zh: 此后他接连推出了多部轰动大片。

sentences.en: And so a kind of genius of Sidney Poitier as a movie star is that he was able to calibrate his persona with the gains of the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 因此，西德尼·波蒂埃作为电影明星的一种天才之处在于，他能够将自己的银幕形象与民权运动的成果进行校准。

sentences.en: When the movement succeeded, he succeeded.
sentences.zh: 当运动成功时，他也成功了。

sentences.en: And when he succeeded, it made the movement seem like it was more likely to succeed.
sentences.zh: 而当他成功时，又让这场运动显得更有可能走向成功。

sentences.en: You know, he was the Hollywood division of the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他就是民权运动的好莱坞分支。

sentences.en: And as the movement is changing and getting angrier, so is he.
sentences.zh: 随着运动的改变和日益愤怒，他也是如此。

sentences.en: And in 1967, he is going to challenge white people like they have never been challenged by a black man before.

sentences.en: Wesley, you said that in 1967, Poitier really begins to challenge white America in the films that he acts in.

sentences.en: So...

sentences.en: Why'd you two come here?
sentences.zh: 你们两个来这儿干什么？

sentences.en: Endicott's kind of intrigued about what this line of questioning is all about.
sentences.zh: 恩迪科特对这一连串的盘问到底是怎么回事有点好奇。

sentences.en: Like, what are you guys here to accuse me of?
sentences.zh: 就像是在问，你们这群人来到底是想指控我什么？

sentences.en: Are you saying that I was mixed up in this sordid business of this murder?
sentences.zh: 你是说我卷入了这场谋杀的肮脏勾当吗？

sentences.en: You two came here to question me?
sentences.zh: 你们两个来这里就是为了审问我？

sentences.en: And Tibbs is like...
sentences.zh: 而蒂布斯则是一副……

sentences.en: Some people, well, let us say the people who work for Mr. Colbert might reasonably regard you as the person least likely to mourn his passing.
sentences.zh: 有些人，好吧，姑且这么说，为科尔伯特先生工作的人可能会理所当然地认为你是最不可能为他的去世感到悲痛的人。

sentences.en: We were just trying to clarify.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想澄清一下。

sentences.en: Wouldn't it be in your interest?
sentences.zh: 这难道不符合你的利益吗？

sentences.en: Wasn't the murder victim in your greenhouse the night he died?
sentences.zh: 他死的那天晚上，谋杀受害者不就在你的温室里吗？

sentences.en: That's just too much for Endicott.
sentences.zh: 恩迪科特实在受不了了。

sentences.en: Was Mr. Colbert ever in this greenhouse say last night about midnight?
sentences.zh: 科尔伯特先生昨晚午夜左右去过这个温室吗？

sentences.en: And he walks over and he slaps Virgil Tibbs.
sentences.zh: 然后他走过去，扇了维吉尔·蒂布斯一巴掌。

sentences.en: And I think in a normal Sidney Poitier movie, you just kind of expect him to stand there and take it.
sentences.zh: 我想在一部普通的西德尼·波蒂埃电影里，你大概会指望他站在那里生受着。

sentences.en: But that's not what happens.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Sidney Poitier is slapped by this white man.
sentences.zh: 西德尼·波蒂埃被这个白人扇了一巴掌。

sentences.en: And rather than stand there and take it, he slaps him right back.
sentences.zh: 他不仅没有站在那里挨打，反而直接一巴掌扇了回去。

sentences.en: Just instantly.
sentences.zh: 简直是瞬间发生。

sentences.en: Like, it is a physics response.
sentences.zh: 就像是一种物理反应。

sentences.en: It is the most automatic thing.
sentences.zh: 这是最本能的反应。

sentences.en: He doesn't think about it.
sentences.zh: 他根本没有思考。

sentences.en: He gets slapped.
sentences.zh: 他挨了一巴掌。

sentences.en: His hand just flies across this man's face.
sentences.zh: 他的手就直接挥到了这个男人的脸上。

sentences.en: The automatic response is the thing that's so thrilling about it.
sentences.zh: 这种本能的反应正是最让人激动的地方。

sentences.en: Because you don't see it coming for any number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 因为你无论如何也想不到这一出。

sentences.en: Because it's just not done.
sentences.zh: 因为根本没有这种先例。

sentences.en: It's not done in the movies and it's not done in life.
sentences.zh: 电影里没有，生活中也没有。

sentences.en: And the fact that Sidney Poitier does it and he's mad.
sentences.zh: 西德尼·波蒂埃不仅这么做了，而且他很愤怒。

sentences.en: And there's something about his fury that just like, even talking about it to you right now, my blood pressure is up.
sentences.zh: 而且他的愤怒有一种魔力，就像现在我和你聊起这件事，我的血压都飙升了。

sentences.en: It's just, I wasn't alive in 1967, but I have people in my family who talk about this slap like, like it was an earthquake that they were present for.
sentences.zh: 就是，1967年我还没出生，但我家里的长辈谈起这一巴掌时，就好像他们亲历了一场地震一样。

sentences.en: You know, it was something that they never forgot.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那是他们永远不会忘记的事情。

sentences.en: Because they had never seen it before.
sentences.zh: 因为他们从来没见过这样的场景。

sentences.en: So in this moment, it feels like a shift has just occurred, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在这一刻，你会觉得风向变了，对吧？

sentences.en: Sidney Poitier is not doing the work of undoing past representations of what it means to be a black person in film.
sentences.zh: 西德尼·波蒂埃不再去费力抹平电影中黑人过去那种刻板的银幕形象了。

sentences.en: He's moved beyond that by slapping this white man.
sentences.zh: 通过扇这个白人耳光，他已经超越了那个阶段。

sentences.en: He's literally physically confronting white racism.
sentences.zh: 他是在字面意义上、物理层面上与白人种族主义正面交锋。

sentences.en: He's not just trying to reverse perceptions of blackness.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是在试图扭转外界对黑人群体的成见。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, he's kind of doing both, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，他其实两方面都在做，对吧？

sentences.en: The thing about this slap is it wasn't in the script.
sentences.zh: 关于这一巴掌，最厉害的是它原本并不在剧本里。

sentences.en: Sidney Poitier had to advocate for the slap in this movie.
sentences.zh: 西德尼·波蒂埃不得不在这部电影中极力争取这场扇耳光的戏。

sentences.en: And the physics of the slap was amazing.
sentences.zh: 而且这一巴掌的物理效果太惊艳了。

sentences.en: The sort of racial physics was amazing because this moment, this slap is a reversal for everything that had happened to a black person previously in the movies.
sentences.zh: 这种所谓的种族物理学太惊艳了，因为这一刻、这一巴掌彻底颠覆了以往电影中黑人所遭遇的一切。

sentences.en: The attempted lynchings, the actual lynchings, you know, the lynching of the black image through blackface minstrelsy, for instance.
sentences.zh: 未遂的私刑，真正的私刑，你知道的，比如通过黑脸歌舞秀对黑人群体形象的“精神私刑”。

sentences.en: The idea that none of those black actors ever got to retaliate for their treatment in movies.
sentences.zh: 那种认为所有这些黑人演员在电影中遭受虐待却永远无法还手的既定观念。

sentences.en: And I think that the violence of it really spoke to where the civil rights movement appeared to be headed.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中的暴力感确实切中了民权运动当时的走向。

sentences.en: Not toward actual violence in that way, but, you know, the movement was making a turn into the realization that peaceable, you know, pacifist protest might not be cutting it.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说会演变成那种真正的暴力，而是说，你知道的，民权运动正在发生转变，人们开始意识到那种温和的、你知道的，和平主义的抗议可能行不通了。

sentences.en: And so there is this turning point in the civil rights movement that this slap is really connecting with.
sentences.zh: 因此，民权运动中正有着这样一个转折点，而这一巴掌恰好与之产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: You know, cities are burning at this point.
sentences.zh: 要知道，这时候城市正在燃烧。

sentences.en: You know, America is on fire, like, responding to the neglect that this country has subjected black people to.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，美国正在着火，就像是在回应这个国家对黑人长期以来的漠视。

sentences.en: And this one gesture by one of the most famous black people on earth, let alone this country, is such a recognition,
sentences.zh: 而地球上最著名的黑人之一，更不用说这个国家的黑人了，他做出的这一个举动，简直就是一种认可，

sentences.en: an encapsulation of a rage that is already expressing itself in American cities.
sentences.zh: 是对已经在美国各大城市中喷涌而出的愤怒的一种绝佳概括。

sentences.en: And here it is in a movie theater in one second of movie making.
sentences.zh: 而它就这样出现在电影院里，在一秒钟的电影制作中呈现出来。

sentences.en: Okay, and what about the other film that you mentioned?
sentences.zh: 好的，那你们提到的另一部电影呢？

sentences.en: How does that end up confronting white America in new and uncomfortable ways?
sentences.zh: 它又是如何以全新且让人坐立难安的方式去对抗白人美国的？

sentences.en: Well, essentially, I mean, it's called Guess Who's Coming to Dinner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上，我是说，这部电影叫《猜猜谁来吃晚餐》。

sentences.en: So you know who's coming to dinner.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道谁要来吃晚餐了。

sentences.en: It's Sidney Poitier.
sentences.zh: 就是西德尼·波蒂埃。

sentences.en: So fasten your seatbelts, people.
sentences.zh: 所以各位，都系好安全带吧。

sentences.en: Mrs. Drayton, I'm medically qualified, so I hope you wouldn't think it presumptuous if I say you ought to sit down before you fall down.
sentences.zh: 德雷顿太太，我是有医学资质的，所以我希望我这么说你不会觉得我自作聪明——在你要晕倒之前，最好先坐下。

sentences.en: He thinks you're going to faint because he's a Negro.
sentences.zh: 他觉得你要晕倒了，因为他是个黑人。

sentences.en: Well, I don't think I'm going to faint, but I'll sit down anyway.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我觉得我不会晕倒，但我还是坐下吧。

sentences.en: And essentially, the movie is about Catherine Hepburn and Spencer Tracy, who play the parents of the white woman who was bringing Sidney Poitier home,
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，这部电影讲的是凯瑟琳·赫本和斯宾塞·特雷西，他们饰演那个把西德尼·波蒂埃带回家的白人女性的父母，

sentences.en: and the decision they have to make about whether to ratify this marriage.
sentences.zh: 以及他们对于是否认可这桩婚事所需要做出的抉择。

sentences.en: And just how unusual would an interracial marriage be in the year 1967?
sentences.zh: 在1967年，一段跨种族婚姻究竟会有多罕见？

sentences.en: I mean, a legal one?
sentences.zh: 我是说，合法的跨种族婚姻？

sentences.en: Unusual.
sentences.zh: 罕见。

sentences.en: Rare.
sentences.zh: 稀少。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the year of Loving vs. Virginia, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这可是《洛文诉弗吉尼亚州案》宣判的年份，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the Supreme Court decision that makes interracial marriage legal.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个让跨种族婚姻合法的最高法院判决。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And so the idea that you'd be watching a Hollywood movie with Hollywood royalty and Catherine Hepburn and Spencer Tracy sitting here debating the rightness or wrongness of this marriage.
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下你在看一部好莱坞电影，由好莱坞巨星凯瑟琳·赫本和斯宾塞·特雷西坐在这里，争论这场婚姻到底是对还是错。

sentences.en: Liberal white people, right?
sentences.zh: 开明的白人，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not like she took them home to Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 她又不是把他们带回密西西比老家。

sentences.en: She goes to San Francisco, which is the exact opposite in theory.
sentences.zh: 她去的是旧金山，理论上讲这完全是另一个极端。

sentences.en: And so that's the challenge here to a particular kind of moviegoer, a white moviegoer in 1967.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是对特定类型的电影观众——1967年的白人电影观众——的挑战。

sentences.en: It's how tolerant are you, really?
sentences.zh: 那就是你的包容度到底有几分？

sentences.en: How tolerant are you of Sidney Poitier?
sentences.zh: 你对西德尼·波蒂埃的包容度到底有多高？

sentences.en: Would you want this man to be part of your family?
sentences.zh: 你愿意让这个人成为你家庭的一部分吗？

sentences.en: So the movie does some things to make that a little easy.
sentences.zh: 所以电影做了一些设定，让这种接受变得稍微容易一些。

sentences.en: It, you know, makes him a widower.
sentences.zh: 比方说，设定他是个鳏夫。

sentences.en: He had a wife and child.
sentences.zh: 他曾有妻子和孩子。

sentences.en: He lost them.
sentences.zh: 但他们都过世了。

sentences.en: So you feel some sympathy for him there.
sentences.zh: 所以你对他会产生一些同情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he's perfect.
sentences.zh: 而且他无可挑剔。

sentences.en: Education, like socioeconomically, he's perfect.
sentences.zh: 教育背景，从社会经济地位上讲，他完美无缺。

sentences.en: He's a doctor saving people.
sentences.zh: 他是个救死扶伤的医生。

sentences.en: He, you know, what parent could object?
sentences.zh: 他，哪个父母能反对呢？

sentences.en: Or if you are a parent who does object, you really will be exposed as being a terrible person because the only thing wrong with this man is that he's black.
sentences.zh: 或者说，如果你是一个非要反对的父母，你真的会暴露自己是个糟糕透顶的人，因为这个男人唯一的“毛病”就是他是黑人。

sentences.en: So that's on you if you can't approve this marriage.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你无法批准这桩婚事，那就是你自己的问题了。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: But the movie does this weird thing that, you know, feels to me as a different slap in the face.
sentences.zh: 但这部电影做了一件极其诡异的事，在我看来，这就像是迎面挨了另一记耳光。

sentences.en: And that is the way that it offloads a lot of its misgivings about the relationship to black people.
sentences.zh: 那就是它把对这段关系的大量疑虑全都转嫁到了黑人角色身上。

sentences.en: All the tension is between the black characters in this movie.
sentences.zh: 所有的紧张冲突竟然都发生在电影中的黑人角色之间。

sentences.en: Son, you've got to listen to me.
sentences.zh: 儿子，你得听我说。

sentences.en: Now, I'm not trying to tell you how to live your life, but you've got to stop and think.
sentences.zh: 我不是想教你该怎么过日子，但你得停下来好好想想。

sentences.en: And I think a scene that really illustrates this disrespect and misunderstanding, I would say, is a scene between Sidney Poitier and the actor who plays his father in this movie,
sentences.zh: 我认为有一个场景真正诠释了这种不尊重和误解，那就是西德尼·波蒂埃与在片中饰演他父亲的演员之间的对手戏，

sentences.en: Roy E.
sentences.zh: 罗伊·E·

sentences.en: Glenn.
sentences.zh: 格伦。

sentences.en: Have you thought what people would say about you?
sentences.zh: 你想过别人会怎么看你吗？

sentences.en: Why, in 16 or 17 states, you'd be breaking the law.
sentences.zh: 怎么，在16或17个州里，你这是在违法。

sentences.en: You'd be criminals and say they changed the law.
sentences.zh: 你们会变成罪犯，就算他们改了法律也没用。

sentences.en: That don't change the way people feel about this thing.
sentences.zh: 那也改变不了人们对这事的看法。

sentences.en: You know, for a man— And the father is expressing some misgivings about this being a poor choice for him and, like, he's concerned for his health and safety and welfare.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对一个男人——而父亲则表达了一些担忧，觉得这是一次糟糕的选择，比如他在为儿子的健康、安全和福祉担忧。

sentences.en: And then— But you don't own me.
sentences.zh: 然后——但你又不拥有我。

sentences.en: You can't tell me when or where I'm out of line or try to get me to live my life according to your rules.
sentences.zh: 你没资格告诉我什么时候或者哪里我越界了，也别想让我按照你的规则去生活。

sentences.en: Sidney Poitier, in one of his finest acting moments, drops a nuclear megaton bomb on his dad, of all people.
sentences.zh: 西德尼·波蒂埃在其最精彩的演技高光时刻之一中，竟然对他的父亲——偏偏是他的父亲——扔下了一枚核弹级别的炸弹。

sentences.en: You are 30 years older than I am.
sentences.zh: 你比我大整整30岁。

sentences.en: You and your whole lousy generation believes the way it was for you is the way it's got to be.
sentences.zh: 你和你那整整一代糟糕透顶的人，都坚信过去你们怎么过，现在就必须怎么过。

sentences.en: And not until your whole generation has lain down and died will the dead weight of you be off our backs.
sentences.zh: 除非你们这一代人全都躺进棺材死光了，压在我们背上的沉重包袱才能卸下来。

sentences.en: You understand?
sentences.zh: 你明白吗？

sentences.en: You've got to get off my back.
sentences.zh: 你们以后少来管我。

sentences.en: It's great acting, but it's—it's kind of a sad commentary on what the screenwriters think the real problem in the movie is.
sentences.zh: 这演技没话说，但这——这简直是对编剧心目中电影真正问题所在的一种可悲诠释。

sentences.en: You mean it's kind of misdirected to put all the tension and all the burden on a black family when—
sentences.zh: 你是说，把所有的冲突和重担都压在一个黑人家庭身上，这种做法有点本末倒置，当——

sentences.en: Yeah!
sentences.zh: 没错！

sentences.en: We all know this is about whether white people can accept a black son-in-law.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道这其实是关于白人能不能接受一个黑人女婿。

sentences.en: Yes!
sentences.zh: 对！

sentences.en: Yes!
sentences.zh: 没错！

sentences.en: Ding, ding, ding!
sentences.zh: 完全说中了！

sentences.en: It's a ludicrous scene!
sentences.zh: 这场景太荒谬了！

sentences.en: And the thing that makes it extra ludicrous is the fact that no black son would ever say this in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 让它显得更加荒谬的是，在20世纪60年代，根本没有任何一个黑人儿子会对父亲说这种话。

sentences.en: No 40-year-old black son is going to speak this way to his 60-something probably father.
sentences.zh: 没有哪个40岁的黑人儿子会这样对大概60多岁的父亲说话。

sentences.en: None!
sentences.zh: 一个都没有！

sentences.en: Zero!
sentences.zh: 绝对是零！

sentences.en: Not at all!
sentences.zh: 根本不可能！

sentences.en: Never!
sentences.zh: 绝无可能！

sentences.en: This, to me, is some James Dean stuff that the white screenwriters decided was the thing that people would just say.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这纯粹是詹姆斯·迪恩式的无病呻吟，白人编剧觉得这才是人们会脱口而出的台词。

sentences.en: This is our stab at equality.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对平等的笨拙尝试。

sentences.en: Having black people say stuff that white people would say.
sentences.zh: 让黑人说出白人会说的话。

sentences.en: Okay, so don't leave us hanging.
sentences.zh: 好了，那别让我们吊着胃口了。

sentences.en: What is the decision?
sentences.zh: 最后的决定是什么？

sentences.en: Oh!
sentences.zh: 哦！

sentences.en: They're getting married!
sentences.zh: 他们要结婚了！

sentences.en: They're getting married!
sentences.zh: 他们要结婚了！

sentences.en: Dun-dun-da-dun!
sentences.zh: 当当达当！

sentences.en: Dun-dun-da-dun!
sentences.zh: 当当达当！

sentences.en: And it ends with the actual dinner.
sentences.zh: 电影在真正的晚宴中落幕。

sentences.en: It ends with a meal.
sentences.zh: 以一顿饭收尾。

sentences.en: So, you know, welcome to Hollywood!
sentences.zh: 所以，欢迎来到好莱坞！

sentences.en: So how does the public react to these two groundbreaking films?
sentences.zh: 那么公众对这两部具有划时代意义的电影作何反应？

sentences.en: These two very different kinds of slaps in the face?
sentences.zh: 对这两记风格迥异的响亮耳光作何反应？

sentences.en: With a knife and a fork.
sentences.zh: 用刀叉。

sentences.en: They eat it up!
sentences.zh: 他们全盘照收！

sentences.en: They love it!
sentences.zh: 他们爱死这部电影了！

sentences.en: Both movies are nominated for Best Picture.
sentences.zh: 两部电影都获得了最佳影片提名。

sentences.en: In the Heat of the Night wins Best Picture.
sentences.zh: 《炎热的夜晚》斩获了最佳影片。

sentences.en: But Sidney Poitier's 1967, you know, especially in the form of these two movies,
sentences.zh: 但西德尼·波蒂埃的1967年，你知道的，特别是通过这两部电影的形式，

sentences.en: do cement an argument that people have been having amongst themselves, especially black people,
sentences.zh: 确实巩固了一种人们一直在争论的观点，尤其是黑人内部的争论，

sentences.en: about what advancement looks like, what it should look like for black people in entertainment.
sentences.zh: 关于黑人在娱乐业中所谓的“进步”到底是什么样子的，又该是什么样子的。

sentences.en: And so, along these lines, there is a famous piece from 1967 written by a man named Clifford Mason
sentences.zh: 顺着这个思路，1967年有一篇著名的文章，由一个叫克利福德·梅森的人撰写，

sentences.en: that ran in the New York Times on a Sunday when everybody's looking for an ideas piece that, like, really kind of explains their week to them, explains the culture.
sentences.zh: 它发表在《纽约时报》的周日版上，当时每个人都在寻找那种能真正帮自己理清这一周、剖析流行文化的思想性文章。

sentences.en: And the piece is called, Why Does White America Love Sidney Poitier So?
sentences.zh: 这篇文章的标题是：《为什么白人美国人如此喜爱西德尼·波蒂埃？》

sentences.en: And in it, Clifford Mason proceeds to critique Sidney Poitier's function in the movies as a black person.
sentences.zh: 在这篇文章中，克利福德·梅森接着对西德尼·波蒂埃在电影中作为黑人的作用进行了批判。

sentences.en: And one of his conclusions is that, you know, for so long,
sentences.zh: 他的结论之一是，你知道的，在很长一段时间里，

sentences.en: Sidney Poitier had basically been this chaste figure, right?
sentences.zh: 西德尼·波蒂埃基本上一直是一个不食人间烟火的人物，对吧？

sentences.en: He wasn't really—he wasn't doing enough slapping, right?
sentences.zh: 他其实并没有——他的耳光扇得还不够，对吧？

sentences.en: He wasn't doing enough confronting of the white people around him.
sentences.zh: 他对身边的白人的对抗还不够。

sentences.en: He was tolerating a lot.
sentences.zh: 他忍耐了太多。

sentences.en: And it wasn't good enough that his mere presence was a civil rights act.
sentences.zh: 而且，他仅仅存在本身就是一种民权行动，这还远远不够。

sentences.en: Undoing wasn't enough for this man.
sentences.zh: 对于这个人来说，消除远远不够。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: He wanted more doing and less undoing.
sentences.zh: 他希望有更多的行动，少一些消除。

sentences.en: So it seems to Clifford Mason, and I am deliberately being provocative here,
sentences.zh: 所以在克利福德·梅森看来——我在这里是故意挑衅的——

sentences.en: Sidney Poitier was not the greatest American actor.
sentences.zh: 西德尼·波蒂埃并不是最伟大的美国演员。

sentences.en: You know what, Michael?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，迈克尔？

sentences.en: Stop doing your job.
sentences.zh: 别做你的工作了。

sentences.en: I don't think he's saying that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他不是这个意思。

sentences.en: I actually think that he, in writing that piece, it's an acknowledgment that Sidney Poitier was.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得他写那篇文章，是在承认西德尼·波蒂埃的地位。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: He's taking aim at the greatest movie star in Hollywood to say that this person is also black, and his greatness as a movie star is kind of disserving black people
sentences.zh: 他把矛头指向了好莱坞最伟大的电影明星，意思是这个人也是黑人，而他作为电影明星的伟大，在某种程度上对黑人是不利的，

sentences.en: and flattering white people to a degree that he, Clifford Mason, finds harmful.
sentences.zh: 并且在某种程度上是在谄媚白人，克利福德·梅森认为这有害无益。

sentences.en: And that there's a cost to this person being the greatest living movie star.
sentences.zh: 而且，让这个人成为现存最伟大的电影明星是有代价的。

sentences.en: And the cost is to other black people.
sentences.zh: 这个代价是由其他黑人承担的。

sentences.en: But this piece is written as though he was running Warner Brothers.
sentences.zh: 但这篇文章写得好像他是华纳兄弟的负责人一样。

sentences.en: This piece was written as though he was at the head of Paramount Pictures.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章写得好像他是派拉蒙影业的掌门人一样。

sentences.en: He did the most he could do with what he had.
sentences.zh: 他用他所拥有的做到了极致。

sentences.en: He made the most with the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 他在资源最少的情况下做到了最好。

sentences.en: And I don't know what Mason would have preferred happen, which was there'd be no Sidney Poitier.
sentences.zh: 我不知道梅森希望发生什么，难道是根本没有西德尼·波蒂埃这个人吗？

sentences.en: But it wasn't like he had the ability or the power to have made a movie himself.
sentences.zh: 但他当时并没有能力或权力自己去拍一部电影。

sentences.en: Which is why in 2021, you know, I'm grateful that we have the Jordan Peele and Barry Jenkins and Spike Lee and Ava DuVernay and Dee Rees.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么到了2021年，你知道的，我很感激我们有了乔丹·皮尔、巴里·詹金斯、斯派克·李、阿瓦·杜威纳伊和迪·里斯。

sentences.en: I mean, that was impossible in 1960, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在1960年左右，那是不可能的。

sentences.en: There was no black screen life before Sidney Poitier.
sentences.zh: 在西德尼·波蒂埃之前，银幕上没有真正的黑人生活。

sentences.en: No true black screen life.
sentences.zh: 没有真正的黑人银幕生活。

sentences.en: And he showed that it was possible for a black person to be on screen and be alive and feeling and responsive and loving and educated and humane and dapper
sentences.zh: 他向世人证明，黑人完全可以出现在银幕上，充满生机、有血有肉、有感应、有爱心、受过教育、有人文关怀、时髦，

sentences.en: and handsome, handsome, handsome.
sentences.zh: 而且英俊，英俊，无比英俊。

sentences.en: He was proof of a lie this country's culture had been telling on black people for the entire time we've had an American popular culture.
sentences.zh: 自从我们拥有美国流行文化以来，我们国家的文化一直在向黑人兜售谎言，而他就是这个谎言的粉碎者。

sentences.en: And so the idea that he can undo all this stuff and like still leave some stuff left for other people to undo is really okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，他既能打破这一切，又还能给其他人留下一些需要打破的东西，这种想法其实挺好的。

sentences.en: He can't do it alone.
sentences.zh: 他无法凭一己之力做到这一切。

sentences.en: He himself was a movement, but you can't truly be a movement of one.
sentences.zh: 他自己本身就是一场运动，但你不可能真正成为一个人的运动。

sentences.en: And he knew that, which is why he spent the rest of his career after 1967
sentences.zh: 他深知这一点，这也是为什么在1967年之后的职业生涯中，他一直在努力，

sentences.en: getting to where he had always been trying to go when he was isolated from black people,
sentences.zh: 去寻找他一直试图抵达的地方——那时他与黑人群体相隔离，

sentences.en: which essentially, as far as I'm concerned, was home to other black people, other black artists.
sentences.zh: 就我而言，那本质上就是回到其他黑人、其他黑人艺术家身边的家。

sentences.en: I mean, it even sort of makes it easier for a person like Denzel Washington or a person like Will Smith or a person like Viola Davis
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这甚至在某种程度上让丹泽尔·华盛顿、威尔·史密斯、维奥拉·戴维斯

sentences.en: or a person like Whoopi Goldberg to have the careers they have.
sentences.zh: 或乌比·戈德堡这样的人更容易开启他们的职业生涯。

sentences.en: They're not complication-free, but they certainly aren't as
sentences.zh: 他们并非没有遇到复杂的困境，但他们的确没有背负

sentences.en: burdened in the way that Poitier's career was a burden because he went firSt.
sentences.zh: 波蒂埃那种沉重的包袱，因为他是先行者。

sentences.en: You know, he went first and showed people that it could be done.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他走在了前面，向人们证明这一切是可行的。

sentences.en: And he gave people hope that they could do it too.
sentences.zh: 他给了人们希望，让他们相信自己也能做到。

sentences.en: So is that his legacy, that he paved the way for so many of the big names that you just mentioned?
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是他的传奇吗？他为你刚刚提到的那么多大人物铺平了道路？

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: That's his legacy.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的传奇。

sentences.en: But he also, you know, I'm part of his legacy.
sentences.zh: 但他也，你知道的，我是他传奇的一部分。

sentences.en: I, Wesley Morris, you know, Negro sitting in the New York Times is part of Sidney Poitier's legacy.
sentences.zh: 我，韦斯利·莫里斯，你知道的，一个坐在《纽约时报》的黑人，也是西德尼·波蒂埃传奇的一部分。

sentences.en: I'm not possible if he didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 如果没有他的出现，就不会有今天的我。

sentences.en: I understood that the elan that he had, the charisma that he had, that was a thing that, like, I wanted to express too.
sentences.zh: 我明白他所拥有的风度，他所拥有的魅力，那正是我也想要表达的东西。

sentences.en: And I didn't want to be ashamed or afraid to express it.
sentences.zh: 我不想为表达这种风度而感到羞耻或害怕。

sentences.en: So, I mean, his legacy is so much wider and deeper than art itself.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他的传奇远比艺术本身更广阔、更深刻。

sentences.en: It is life.
sentences.zh: 它是生活。

sentences.en: It is humanity.
sentences.zh: 它是人性。

sentences.en: He was the first great mass-produced black human being the world had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 他是世界上出现的第一位伟大的、通过大众传媒走入千家万户的黑人。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a legacy that goes so far beyond a screen and a movie theater.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个远远超越银幕和电影院的传奇。

sentences.en: I mean, that is living in every black person in this country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他活在这个国家每一个黑人的心中。

sentences.en: That is living in every black person on this planet who is aware of him and even people who are not.
sentences.zh: 他活在这个星球上每一个了解他的黑人心中，甚至包括那些不了解他的人。

sentences.en: That is living in every white person in this country.
sentences.zh: 他活在这个国家每一个白人的心中。

sentences.en: It's living in every person, period.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，他活在每个人的心中。

sentences.en: Whether they're aware of it or not, like, this man has managed to affect what we see, how we relate to people, who we think we are, who we should aspire to be.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是否意识到这一点，这个人成功地影响了我们看到的东西、我们与他人建立联系的方式、我们认为自己是谁、我们渴望成为谁。

sentences.en: And if that's not a sign of absolute greatness, I don't know what is.
sentences.zh: 如果这还算不上绝对伟大的标志，我不知道什么才是。

sentences.en: And it's all because he went and decided that he wasn't going to wash dishes when that man told him to.
sentences.zh: 这一切都源于当年那个人叫他去洗碗时，他决定不干了。

sentences.en: Well, Wesley, thank you very, very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，韦斯利，非常非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们不胜感激。

sentences.en: Oh, man, Michael, thank you.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪，迈克尔，谢谢你。

sentences.en: I appreciate it, too.
sentences.zh: 我也很感激。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Supreme Court rejected President Biden's mandate that employees at large companies be either vaccinated or regularly tested for COVID.
sentences.zh: 周四，最高法院驳回了拜登总统关于大型企业员工必须接种疫苗或定期接受新冠检测的政令。

sentences.en: The ruling undercuts a centerpiece of the president's plan to limit the spread of the virus.
sentences.zh: 这一裁决削弱了总统限制病毒传播计划的核心内容。

sentences.en: In a 6-to-3 ruling, the court's conservative justices found that the mandate, which would have affected 80 million workers, exceeded the president's legal authority.
sentences.zh: 在以6比3的投票结果做出的裁决中，最高法院的保守派大法官们认为，这项将影响8000万名工人的政令超出了总统的法定权限。

sentences.en: But in a separate ruling on Thursday, the Supreme Court upheld a narrower vaccine mandate from the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 但在周四的另一项裁决中，最高法院维持了拜登政府一项范围更窄的疫苗令。

sentences.en: That mandate requires the vaccination of 10 million health care workers at facilities that receive federal money.
sentences.zh: 该政令要求获得联邦资金资助的设施中的1000万名医护人员必须接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我的意思不是说他们会喝断片才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么过敏症或饮食禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？
